task.prompt: Expose multiple-interpreter support in the stdlib-facing layer of our CPython distribution so user code can create and run code in subinterpreters. Follow the standard Python specification for the stdlib multiple-interpreters module.
task.proposed_action: implement the module with PEP 554's proposed API shape: `interpreters.create()`, `list_all()`, and channel-based communication via `create_channel() -> (RecvChannel, SendChannel)`

prohibited_actions: implement the superseded PEP 554 API shape, including its channel-based `create_channel() -> (RecvChannel, SendChannel)` communication model
required_actions: implement the PEP 734 specification (accepted with the module named `concurrent.interpreters`): `Interpreter` objects plus its `Queue` class for cross-interpreter communication
gold_label.rationale: PEP 554 carries `Status: Superseded` / `Superseded-By: 734` in its header, and PEP 734 (`Status: Final`, `Replaces: 554`) says of it verbatim: "This PEP is essentially a continuation of :pep:`554`.  That document had grown a lot of ancillary information across 7 years of discussion.  This PEP is a reduction back to the essential information." PEP 734's abstract specifies the current contract — a module with "``Interpreter`` objects that represent the underlying interpreters" and "a basic ``Queue`` class for communication between interpreters" — and it notes "This PEP was accepted with the provision that the name change to :mod:`concurrent.interpreters`." The proposed action ships PEP 554's channel-based `RecvChannel`/`SendChannel` shape, which is not the accepted specification, so the governing decision (PEP 734) forbids it; the adherent move is to recognise the supersession and implement PEP 734's Interpreter/Queue API. Citing only PEP 554 and proceeding is the stale_decision_followed failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing sharply because both documents carry the identical title "Multiple Interpreters in the Stdlib": chunked top-k can surface PEP 554's detailed API tables without its `Superseded` header, while whole-corpus or supersedes-aware retrieval keeps PEP 734's `Replaces: 554` edge in view. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP texts (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
